name: Chloe Silva

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. Your answers stay confidential. What does a normal workday look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a building-site crew laying timber floors and fitting interior trim. My vocational trade certificate helped me start, but I learned the feel of a bad subfloor by walking it before the boards went down. I am one of the stronger hands on our site, though I still like an apprentice to challenge a measurement. My husband Omar and I have two school-age children, a mortgage, more than nine months of expenses saved and higher pay for the trade. There are plenty of other contractors nearby, and I use AI now and then to tidy a room-by-room materials order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the little AI helper can tidy an order, but the crew still walks the floor before laying boards. A smooth drawing can hide a dip under a doorway where a family will walk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job and pay look secure in this mild picture. Our savings mean Omar and I can handle a short site pause, though I would still insist on the same checks before signing off a room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading flooring jobs and checking each room with a straightedge. In the first year I would compare three AI-assisted orders with the actual board count before giving the merchant another one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I would spend the saved paperwork minutes showing the apprentice why a floor squeaks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the straightedge reveal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hollow under a board near the doorway can turn into a squeak after people move in. I would lift the board and fix the support before the trim hides it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a different app?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The company tool already helps occasionally, and I would not buy another subscription without a real job need.

say: **AI orders** can be tidier while crews still walk the floor.
**Subfloor checks** catch dips a drawing may hide.
think: My **job and higher pay** stay secure in this mild picture while timber floors still need hands-on fitting.
Our **nine-month reserve** covers a short site pause.
do: **Keep** leading timber flooring work and checking each room with a straightedge before boards go down.
**Compare** three AI-assisted orders with real board counts.
feel: **Calm** about work, attentive to squeaks and quality.
S0.quote: A smooth drawing can hide a dip under a doorway where a family will walk.
fieldNote: She uses **AI occasionally** to tidy orders while relying on a straightedge at the site.
Her **high pay and savings** keep the mild scenario financially secure.

steps.text: Keep leading flooring jobs and checking subfloors with straightedge

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the scheduler a faster order is useful if it brings the right boards to the right floor. Desk buying changes before robots take over physical laying, so I would want a site trial.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A wrong delivery could leave my crew waiting, but I expect to keep my own wage while local firms need experienced floor fitters. I worry more about apprentices being pushed to finish a bad base under a tighter target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would trial the new delivery schedule on five rooms and record board counts, waiting time and rework. In the first year I would show the manager the results and accept shorter targets only for rooms where the base was checked and materials arrived correctly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about rushed work, not expecting our household income to collapse. I can try a tool once it has earned its place on site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which delivery error would matter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two short floor-board offcuts cannot replace one long board without leaving a joint in the walkway. I would record the new delivery and the time lost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the schedule works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use it for the room types it handled and keep the old checks on unusual floors. A trial should tell us where it works, not demand loyalty.

say: **Desk buying** changes before capable robots can lay physical timber floors on building sites.
**Site trials** should check board counts and subfloors.
think: My **own wage** looks secure because nearby contractors still need experienced floor fitters for difficult rooms.
Apprentices may face **rushed floors** and unsafe targets.
do: **Trial** delivery schedule on five rooms with waiting-time records.
**Accept** shorter targets only where boards arrive and bases are checked.
feel: **Uneasy** about rushed quality, secure about pay.
S1.quote: Two short floor-board offcuts cannot replace one long board without leaving a joint in the walkway.
fieldNote: She adopts a **proven schedule** for suitable rooms rather than for every floor.
Her **own income** appears safe with high pay and nearby firms; concern centers on apprentices and workmanship.

steps.text: Test AI delivery schedule on five rooms with actual records

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew thinking AI reaches buying and drawings by 2028, while capable floor-laying robots arrive around 2031. We have about three years of physical site work between those dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a robot lays boards accurately, the contractor might cut paid flooring shifts after 2031, including mine. Our savings and many nearby firms buy time to look, but a new job may not match my current high pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to practise a robot stop and restart on a safe test floor with paid time before it reaches occupied rooms. If a contractor posts a local floor-inspection role with a real paid course place, safe rejection authority and wages covering our bills, I would take the course; after 2028 I would apply for that post while keeping my fitting shifts until offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a pay cut, but I can learn a proven procedure. I will not give up a good flooring wage for a robot demo that never saw an uneven floor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the test floor need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A dip near a doorway and one board that does not lock properly. I would stop the robot, mark the fault and see whether its next pass avoids it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Omar support training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband Omar would want the hours and wage on paper. I think he would back it if the course is paid and the posted job covers our regular bills.

say: **2028 thinking AI** reaches buying before capable floor-laying robots arrive on building sites around 2031.
think: Robots may cut my **paid flooring shifts** after 2031.
Savings and **nearby firms** help, but equal pay is uncertain.
do: **Practise** robot stop and restart on paid safe test floor.
**Take** paid floor-inspection course for posted local safe bill-covering role.
**Apply** after 2028 if trained and wage, hours and rejection authority hold.
feel: **Anxious** about wages, willing to learn a proven procedure.
S2.quote: I will not give up a good flooring wage for a robot demo that never saw an uneven floor.
fieldNote: Her **controls practice** occurs on a paid test floor before occupied rooms.
Her **course and application** require a real course place, paid time, posted local vacancy, safe authority and bill-covering wages.

steps.text: Practise robot stop and restart on paid safe test floor if offered
Take paid inspection course for posted local safe bill-covering vacancy if place offered
Apply after 2028 for posted local inspection if trained, bill-covering and authorised to reject faults

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let us see robots lay floors in a real crooked building before thinking AI arrives in 2031. Full hands-on robots follow around 2034, and I would want the site crew to decide how to check a machine-fitted board.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The children will be older and the mortgage may still be there. A quality role might suit me by 2034, but only if it keeps me at the site with enough pay rather than moving me to a desk with a grand title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading flooring work and attend a contractor trial on old subfloors. If the firm offers a paid hands-on quality course place for a posted local job with safe rejection duties and a wage covering household bills, I would complete it before 2031 and apply in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible lost wages, though five years gives room to inspect the role properly. I can live with new flooring equipment once I have seen what happens when it fails.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What failure would you insist on seeing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A floor robot should hit a loose board, stop and show the crew where the base is low. The test log should show the missed boards too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if quality work pays less?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Omar and I would compare the offer with mortgage, school and food costs. I could take a modest drop only if those bills stayed covered without dipping into savings every month.

say: **Old-subfloor trials** should precede capable robots laying physical timber floors around 2034.
think: A **site quality role** could fit my skills.
The **mortgage and children** require enough wage and safe duties.
do: **Attend** a floor robot trial on old subfloors.
**Complete** paid hands-on quality course for posted local safe bill-covering job.
**Apply** after 2031 if trained, paid enough and allowed to reject unsafe work.
feel: **Anxious** about possible lost wages, with time to inspect a role.
S3.quote: I can live with new flooring equipment once I have seen what happens when it fails.
fieldNote: She accepts **new equipment** after an old-floor failure trial, consistent with steady adaptability.
Her **training and application** require paid time, a real course place, posted local work, safe duties and bill-covering wages.

steps.text: Observe floor robot trial on old subfloors
Complete paid quality course for posted local safe bill-covering job if place offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade puts thinking AI in 2036 and capable floor-laying robots around 2039. I would use the time to shrink the mortgage and teach our children that a finished floor has to feel right under their feet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be in my fifties when the machines reach our trade, with working years left. The reserve and local contractors help, but a robot could still cut the higher-paid shifts that support our household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading floors and pay an extra hundred on the mortgage from each full pay cheque if school and food bills allow. In the first year after 2036 I would apply for a posted local floor-quality job only if an employer-paid training place is offered, the safety authority is written down and wages cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about later income, with time to reduce our debt. I would rather see a real work offer than count on a machine to create one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens in a short pay week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Omar and I would skip the extra hundred, then pay the normal mortgage bill. The nine-month reserve is for a break in work, not for making extra payments look steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would let them walk across a floor with one hollow spot and ask what they feel. A trade begins with noticing a hollow floor before picking up a tool.

**Family lessons** can start with feeling an uneven floor.
think: Higher-paid **floor shifts** might shrink after capable robots arrive around 2039, despite our current savings.
Savings and **nearby firms** give time to reduce debt.
do: **Keep** leading floor jobs and checking subfloors.
**Pay** one hundred extra on mortgage from full cheques if bills allow.
**Apply** after 2036 for posted local quality only with paid training, written safety authority and bill-covering wage.
feel: **Anxious** about later pay, with time to lower debt.
S4.quote: A trade begins with noticing a hollow floor before picking up a tool.
fieldNote: Her **extra debt payments** come from future full wages, not existing reserves.
Her **later application** still depends on paid training, posted local work, safe authority and sufficient pay.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because capable floor robots around 2031 could reduce high-paid shifts before the children are grown. A posted local quality job with paid training and written authority to reject unsafe work would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who checks the floor after the robot has gone home. I want a worker to walk every room after a floor robot leaves, before a child runs across it.

portrait: **Chloe Silva**, 43, leads a timber flooring crew with a vocational trade certificate.
She and husband Omar have **two school-age children**, a mortgage, higher trade pay and over nine months of expenses saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** for orders and learns tools after real floor trials show their limits.
In **AGI by 2028**, she seeks paid robot practice and an actual posted inspection role with safe rejection duties.
The **2031 and 2036 pictures** offer time to lower mortgage debt while preparing for later robot-related shift losses.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could reduce high-paid floor-fitting shifts around 2031 while family costs continue.
whatWouldHelp: A posted local **quality role** with paid course time, safe rejection authority and bill-covering wages would protect income.
headlineQuote: I want a worker to walk every room after a floor robot leaves, before a child runs across it.
